 Home Bharat Himachal Pradesh Himachal Pradesh: ‘Rs 8,555 Cr owed to retirees’: BJP slams Sukhu Govt over unpaid dues; Demand 10% backlog clearance
 Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu announces a 5 per cent dearness allowance hike and Rs 10,000 in arrears for Class IV employees ahead of Deepawali, but employees’ groups, pensioners and the BJP question delayed payments, mounting liabilities and the state’s financial priorities
 S Shukla Oct 27, 2026, 09:00 am IST in Himachal Pradesh Himachal Pradesh’s 5 per cent DA hike sparks questions over pending employee dues, pension delays and the Sukhu government’s finances
 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Telegram Email SHIMLA: The Himachal Pradesh government’s announcement of a 5 per cent dearness allowance (DA) hike for state government employees and pensioners has triggered a wider debate over unpaid financial dues, pension delays and the state’s fiscal management. While Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu has presented the decision as a Diwali relief measure, employee representatives and the opposition BJP argue that the announcement falls short of addressing years of accumulated arrears.
 The additional DA will be paid along with salaries and pensions due on November 1, according to the government’s announcement on Friday. Class IV employees will also receive an instalment of Rs 10,000 towards pending arrears. The Finance Department subsequently issued a notification formalising the decision.
 However, the announcement has renewed questions over the payment of outstanding dues, with employee representatives claiming that the latest increase does not settle the state government’s broader financial obligations.
 A 5 per cent hike against a claimed 10 per cent backlog
 According to former state president of the Akhil Bharatiya Rashtriya Shaikshik Mahasangh, Dr Mamaraj Pundir, the newly announced 5% DA comprises 1 per cent due from July 2023 and 4 per cent due from January 2024. He has raised concerns over reports that payment of the corresponding arrears will be ordered separately at a later date.
 Pundir said employees were still awaiting a cumulative 10 per cent DA linked to several subsequent instalments: 3 per cent from July 2024, 2 per cent from January 2025, 3 per cent from July 2025 and 2 per cent from January 2026.
 He also called for clarity on arrears associated with the pay revision based on the 2016 Pay Commission, along with pending DA payments dating back to July 2022. He urged the government to publish a clear payment schedule, arguing that announcements without actual disbursement offered limited financial relief.
 The government had announced a 3 per cent DA increase in October 2025, when the Centre was reportedly paying its employees approximately 55 per cent DA. The latest state announcement comes amid renewed comparisons with central government benefits. The figures cited by employee representatives, however, require verification against the applicable government orders and payment schedules.
 Pensioners threaten to surround HRTC headquarters
 The financial dispute extends beyond serving government employees. Retired employees of the Himachal Road Transport Corporation (HRTC) have demanded the release of an additional 8 per cent DA and the payment of outstanding pensions and other retirement benefits by October 31.
 The HRTC Pensioners Joint Action Committee has warned that it will surround the corporation’s headquarters on November 3 if its demands remain unmet. Pensioners have also threatened to celebrate Diwali outside the headquarters if necessary.
 At a meeting with HRTC Managing Director Shivam Pratap, pensioners raised their outstanding demands, but no concrete decision was reached. The managing director reportedly assured them that their demands would be placed before the state government, while emphasising that financial resources would be necessary to meet the liabilities.
 Committee secretary Rajendra Thakur alleged that HRTC pensioners were being treated differently from pensioners in other state departments, some of whom had already received a 3 per cent DA instalment.
 He said several employees who retired after December 2025 had been waiting for their pensions for months, with some reportedly facing delays of nearly ten months. The non-payment, pensioners say, has made it increasingly difficult to meet household expenses and basic needs.
 BJP alleges prolonged neglect of employees
 Hamirpur, Himachal Pradesh: BJP MP Anurag Thakur says, “The demands of both pensioners and employees had been pending for several years. Even the salary/pension increases that were approved during our tenure were never disbursed. This government is now nearing the completion of its four-year term. Focusing specifically on pensioners, an amount of Rs 8,555 crore owed to our retired government employees remains unpaid. Similarly, the situation for athletes has dragged on from 2018 to 2026; they have yet to receive the rewards they earned for the medals won at the National Games or at the international level. It is truly unfortunate.”
 BJP MP from Hamirpur and former Union minister Anurag Thakur has criticised the Sukhu government over pending employee and pensioner dues. He claimed that outstanding liabilities had accumulated over several years and cited Rs 8,555 crore in dues relating to employees and pensioners.
 Thakur also questioned the government’s handling of benefits owed to sportspersons, including rewards for medals won at national and international competitions. He argued that the administration was approaching four years in office without resolving several longstanding commitments.
 The opposition has further highlighted previous salary and allowance cuts affecting ministers, legislators and officials, which were subsequently restored in stages, as well as restrictions on promotions for teachers in state universities and colleges dating back to 2020.
 These claims form part of the BJP’s broader attack on the government’s financial management, although the individual amounts and outstanding liabilities require independent verification.
 Also Read: Odisha: PM Modi inaugurates RBI Data Centre and Cybersecurity Institute to strengthen digital financial security Government defends its financial position
 Chief Minister Sukhu has defended his government’s record, saying it has prioritised employees’ interests despite difficult financial circumstances. He reiterated that the government would not discontinue the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), which his administration restored after coming to power.
 Sukhu also said the state was working towards greater financial self-reliance. According to figures cited by him, Himachal Pradesh’s total debt stood at Rs 99,594 crore. He attributed Rs 37,718 crore in borrowings to the period since the Congress government took office, compared with Rs 43,267 crore during the previous BJP government’s tenure.
 These figures do not, by themselves, establish the causes of the state’s financial difficulties. A fuller assessment would require comparisons of borrowing periods, revenue receipts, expenditure, debt servicing and outstanding liabilities.
 Meanwhile, the Himachal Pradesh Pensioners’ Joint Struggle Committee has been conducting awareness programmes at the block level to inform pensioners about their rights and mobilise support for their demands. Its state general secretary, Bhup Singh Verma, said the government should clear the remaining 10% DA arrears before Diwali and warned that demonstrations could take place during
